data.title: bn-3c4d: rite sessions attach/detach records live harness sessions and stakes the agent:// claim

data.body:
[risk:high] Session uniqueness is checked outside the append lock. Two concurrent attach commands can both read an empty session snapshot. The first stakes agent://name. The second then treats that same-agent claim as reusable and records a claimless attachment. Concurrent different agents can also bind one session id twice. Detaching the attachment that staked the claim releases occupancy while another attachment remains live. A responder hook can then cold-spawn beside that live session.

Failure modes: duplicate live attachments, claimless survivors, duplicate delivery targets, and cold-spawn overlap.
Edge cases: same agent with different sessions, different agents with one session, and replace racing attach.
Rollback: disable this session registry or retire duplicate records and claims before restoring hook admission.
Monitoring: detect multiple attached records per case-insensitive agent or exact session, plus attached records without valid occupancy.
Validation: use deterministic process barriers before compare-and-append. Assert exactly one attach succeeds, one live record remains, and one claim exists.

The uniqueness check and append must share one registry lock. Cross-file claim changes also need a recoverable transaction or reservation protocol.

[risk:high] Renewal can revive an expired claim after another holder takes the identity. FileClaim.active remains true after TTL expiry. This branch checks active but not expires_at, then extends the old claim without checking the current pattern holder. The missing or released claim path also checks a stale snapshot and uses append_record instead of atomic append_if. Either path can create two valid agent://name claims.

Failure modes: a stale bridge regains occupancy, two holders coexist, and ownership transfer becomes ambiguous.
Edge cases: expiry followed by another holder, manual release followed by a race, and simultaneous renewers.
Rollback: stop bridge renewal and let claims lapse until the renewal path uses atomic current-holder validation.
Monitoring: flag multiple unexpired active claims for one exact agent pattern and renewals after ownership changed.
Validation: expire the attachment claim, stake the pattern as another agent, then assert renewal fails. Add a barrier race for restake.

Renewal must validate expiry and current ownership under the claims-file compare-and-append lock.

data.reason: Two risk:high races break exclusive agent occupancy: attach uniqueness is not atomic, and renew can resurrect or restake claims over a current holder.

data.body: [risk:high][resolved] The repair now validates current ownership and expiry under the claims-file lock. src/cli/sessions.rs:115-130 extends only the current claim id and stakes only when no holder exists. This closes the expired-claim overwrite and concurrent restake path described above.

data.reason: Atomic current-holder checks at src/cli/sessions.rs:115-130 close this finding.

data.body:
[risk:high] The repair fixes same-file uniqueness, but attachment and occupancy state remain non-atomic. src/cli/sessions.rs:233 makes the attachment live before src/cli/sessions.rs:294 stakes occupancy. A process exit or write failure in that interval leaves a live attachment without an agent claim. A concurrent detach can append the detached record at src/cli/sessions.rs:369 before occupancy exists. Attach then stakes the claim and returns without rechecking, leaving no live attachment but a live claim. Both states silently break responder admission.

Failure modes: duplicate cold spawns beside a live session, or a ghost claim that suppresses a needed spawn.
Edge cases: process exit after session append, disk failure during rollback, detach between session append and claim append, and replace failure after the successor append.
Rollback: disable sessions-based admission and retire inconsistent session and claim records before restoring responder hooks.
Monitoring: alert when each live attachment lacks exactly one effective agent claim, or a session-owned claim lacks one live attachment.
Validation: add deterministic barriers after the session append and before claim append. Force exit, rollback failure, and detach at that point, then assert the invariant in both logs.

Use one recoverable transaction protocol across the two append-only logs. A pending record plus commit or abort recovery can preserve crash consistency.

[risk:high] Replacement transfers the old claim id to the successor at src/cli/sessions.rs:205-211 and retires the old attachment at src/cli/sessions.rs:286-288, but the old record still authorizes release. A detach that read the old record before replacement can later release the transferred claim at src/cli/sessions.rs:369-376. A stale renew of the old attachment can also extend the shared claim, observe the old attachment as detached, and release the successor claim at src/cli/sessions.rs:504-509. The successor remains live while responder admission sees the identity as free.

Failure modes: the successor loses occupancy, a responder cold-spawns beside it, and two live agents process the same work.
Edge cases: late SessionEnd during replace, old-bridge renewal during replace, repeated replace, and release after successor renewal.
Rollback: disable claim transfer during replacement and require the old bridge to stop before attaching the successor.
Monitoring: flag a live attachment whose recorded claim id is inactive, plus release events from an attachment that is no longer the current owner.
Validation: use barriers to pause old detach and old renew before release. Complete replacement, resume the stale operation, and assert the successor claim stays valid.

Bind release authority to the current attachment under the sessions lock, or issue a new claim generation that stale operations cannot release.

data.reason: Two risk:high lifecycle races remain: cross-file attachment and claim updates are not crash-consistent, and stale detach or renew can release a replacement attachment claim.

data.body: [risk:high][resolved] The attachment-owned claim closes this stale-operation path. src/cli/sessions.rs:120-133 conditionally releases only the current owner. src/cli/sessions.rs:172-188 conditionally transfers or extends only from the entitled owner. Detach at src/cli/sessions.rs:587-602 and renew at src/cli/sessions.rs:673-690 therefore cannot mutate a claim after replacement transfers ownership.

[risk:high] The replacement transaction remains crash-unsafe. src/cli/sessions.rs:419-433 transfers claim ownership to the pending successor before src/cli/sessions.rs:437-449 commits it. A process exit there leaves the old attachment live and the claim owned by the pending attachment. After 60 seconds, src/cli/sessions.rs:233-260 retires that pending attachment and releases its claim. The old live harness then has no occupancy gate. Also, responder admission reads claims only. The interval between reservation at src/cli/sessions.rs:348-361 and occupancy at src/cli/sessions.rs:419-433 can cold-spawn beside the physical live session.

Failure modes: the old live session loses occupancy after failed replacement, or a responder starts during initial attachment.
Edge cases: process exit after ownership transfer, commit I/O failure, a claims-lock stall beyond the pending TTL, and message arrival between reserve and occupy.
Rollback: disable replacement and session-based admission until recovery preserves the old owner or commits the successor.
Monitoring: flag live attachments without one effective claim, pending owners whose predecessor remains live, and responder spawns during attachment.
Validation: use deterministic barriers before occupy and after ownership transfer. Trigger admission or terminate the process, then reconcile and assert one live session with one blocking claim.

Record enough replacement intent to restore the old owner after an abandoned successor. Admission must also treat a live pending reservation as busy.

[risk:high] The new owner field does not constrain the existing claim commands. src/cli/claim.rs:276-299 extends every same-agent claim, including a session-owned claim. src/cli/claim.rs:646-664 releases every same-agent claim without checking owner. The documented worker cleanup command, rite claims release --all, therefore removes live session occupancy. A generic refresh can also keep occupancy alive after the bridge stops.

Failure modes: responder cold-spawn beside a live session, or a ghost occupancy claim suppresses needed recovery.
Edge cases: routine end-of-bone cleanup, pattern-specific refresh, release racing attach commit, and mixed clients that ignore owner.
Rollback: disable session-owned claims or prohibit generic refresh and release while any live attachment exists.
Monitoring: report any owner-bound claim changed by a command without the matching attachment id, plus live-session and claim mismatches.
Validation: attach a session, run generic release and refresh as that agent, and assert both refuse the owner-bound claim while session detach and renew still succeed.

Generic claim mutation must skip owner-bound claims. Only the session command with the matching attachment should mutate them.

[risk:high] Session admission fails open on a damaged JSONL record. load_state uses read_records, whose parser skips unreadable lines and returns the remaining state. append_session_if uses the same skip behavior under its uniqueness lock at src/cli/sessions.rs:68-75. A torn attached record can expose the earlier attaching record. After its TTL, reconcile at src/cli/sessions.rs:233-260 retires it and releases occupancy although the harness remains live. A skipped sole record also lets another attachment reuse the agent or session id.

Failure modes: duplicate live agents, cold-spawn overlap, or release of a valid live-session claim after a torn commit record.
Edge cases: partial final writes, invalid UTF-8, a damaged latest event with a valid predecessor, and damage during replacement.
Rollback: stop session-based hook admission when the local session log reports any unreadable record.
Monitoring: surface session-log skipped-line and damaged-field counts as a hard unhealthy state, correlated with claim and attachment mismatches.
Validation: deterministically truncate each attaching, attached, and detached record position. Assert attach, detach, renew, and reconciliation fail closed without releasing or reusing identities.

Security-sensitive session reads must return the scan issues and refuse state-changing decisions when any record is unreadable.

[risk:medium] The host-local session id is copied into the occupancy claim message. That claim is written to claims.jsonl at src/cli/sessions.rs:177-203. Sync stages all data except local at src/sync/git.rs:234-260, so the next sync commit can publish the harness session id although local/sessions.jsonl is excluded. Use a non-identifying claim message, such as live harness session, and keep the exact id only in local state.

data.reason: Three risk:high blockers remain: attachment and replacement crash windows can remove admission; generic claim commands bypass attachment ownership; damaged session records fail open. A risk:medium synced session-id disclosure also remains.

data.body:
[risk:high] The damaged-log repair still has a lock gap. append_session_if checks readability at src/cli/sessions.rs:102-105, then append_if takes the exclusive lock at src/storage/jsonl.rs:355-360 and skips unreadable lines at src/storage/jsonl.rs:382-387. A concurrent writer can acquire the lock after the first check, leave a torn record, and exit. The waiting append then folds the damaged log and can reuse or retire hidden state.

Failure modes: duplicate attachments, hidden live sessions, or release of valid occupancy after a torn concurrent append.
Edge cases: a process exit during attaching, attached, or detached append; a waiter that already passed the precheck; and invalid UTF-8 written before lock handoff.
Rollback: refuse session mutations until the read performed under the append lock reports no scan issues.
Monitoring: treat any session-log skipped line as a hard unhealthy state and correlate it with the next attempted mutation.
Validation: pause one process after the precheck, write a torn record under the lock, resume it, and assert its predicate never runs and nothing appends.

The readability decision must use the same locked snapshot as the conditional append.

[risk:high] The hook-to-session admission race remains. stake_hook_claim checks agent_is_reserved at src/cli/hooks.rs:1121-1124 before it locks and appends the claim at src/cli/hooks.rs:1128-1130. Attach independently reserves under the sessions lock at src/cli/sessions.rs:411-424. A hook can pass its check, attach can reserve, then the hook can stake and spawn. Attach accepts that same-agent ownerless claim at src/cli/sessions.rs:241-244 and commits, so both agents run.

Failure modes: a cold responder overlaps the live harness, duplicate work, and conflicting replies under one identity.
Edge cases: TTL, on-exit, and check-only hook gates; a configured same-agent claim owner; and a message arriving during attach.
Rollback: disable session-aware cold spawning until hook admission and attachment reservation share a recoverable ordering protocol.
Monitoring: flag hook firings whose agent matches an attaching or attached record, plus ownerless agent claims created after a reservation.
Validation: add deterministic barriers after agent_is_reserved and before claim append or Ready. Reserve the session, resume the hook, and assert the hook cannot spawn while attach commits.

The sequential test at tests/sessions.rs:1166-1183 does not exercise this interleaving.

[risk:high] Abandoned replacement recovery can revive an expired claim over a new holder. The handback extends the predecessor claim for at least one second at src/cli/sessions.rs:283-285. Its locked predicate at src/cli/sessions.rs:286-289 checks active and owner only. Expiry leaves active true. After the transferred claim expires, another agent can stake the same pattern, then reconciliation appends this handback and creates two unexpired holders.

Failure modes: two agents hold one identity, the old live harness regains admission, and claim-based consumers choose conflicting owners.
Edge cases: expiry after successor crash, a new holder before reconciliation, the one-second minimum in ttl_remaining, and clock-boundary races.
Rollback: disable replacement handback until it verifies the current pattern holder under the claims lock.
Monitoring: detect multiple unexpired claims for one exact agent pattern and handbacks of already expired claims.
Validation: simulate an abandoned successor owning an expired claim, stake the pattern under a new claim, run reconciliation, and assert no duplicate holder appears.

Handback must require this claim to be the sole current holder. If another claim holds the pattern, recovery must not revive the predecessor.

[risk:high] The generic-claim repair is incomplete for an attachment backed by a pre-existing manual claim. occupy returns HeldByAgent for an ownerless same-agent claim at src/cli/sessions.rs:241-244 and commits the attachment without taking ownership. Generic release skips only claims with owner set at src/cli/claim.rs:669-679, so routine claims release --all can remove the live attachment occupancy.

Failure modes: claim-based admission starts a second agent beside the harness, or downstream status reports the live session as unoccupied.
Edge cases: a manual claim created before attach, a hook claim won during the attach race, release-all cleanup, and manual claim expiry without bridge renewal.
Rollback: refuse attach when occupancy is ownerless, or disable claim-based session admission until ownership is explicit.
Monitoring: flag attached records without exactly one unexpired owner-bound claim and any ownerless agent claim supporting a live attachment.
Validation: stake agent://name manually, attach, run claims release --all, and assert one protected occupancy claim remains and renew owns it.

Every committed attachment needs an owner-bound claim. Ownerless occupancy cannot provide the release and renewal guarantees this repair requires.

[risk:medium][resolved] The synced-identifier leak is fixed. src/cli/sessions.rs:87-89 uses a constant non-identifying claim message, while the exact harness session id remains in local/sessions.jsonl. src/sync/git.rs excludes local state from new and existing data repositories.

data.reason: Fixed at target 7bc5cf6289985f418034a8b52152b4e32b84e914: claim message is non-identifying and local session state is excluded from sync.

risk:high blockers remain: session-log readability is checked outside the append lock; hook admission races attachment reservation across separate logs; replacement handback can revive an expired claim over a new holder; ownerless manual claims can back a committed attachment and remain generically releasable.
The reported mechanisms are repaired at the current target. New residual blockers are tracked in separate threads.

data.body:
[risk:high] Hook admission can still win after a session reserves the identity. stake_hook_claim reads agent_is_reserved at src/cli/hooks.rs:1121-1124, then takes only the claims lock at src/cli/hooks.rs:1128-1130. Attach can reserve between those operations. If the hook appends first, it proceeds to spawn_hook at src/cli/hooks.rs:2092-2102. Attach then refuses the ownerless claim at src/cli/sessions.rs:285-307, but refusal does not terminate the harness that the launcher already started before calling attach. The two agents therefore overlap despite the failed registration.

Failure modes: a cold responder overlaps an already-live harness, performs duplicate work, or sends conflicting replies under one identity.
Edge cases: a launcher that discovers the session id after startup, a message during initial attach, claim TTL and on-exit gates, and attach abort after hook spawn.
Rollback: do not use session registration as a responder admission gate until hook stake and session reservation share one atomic admission protocol.
Monitoring: alert on hook spawns whose identity has a concurrent or immediately aborted attaching record.
Validation: pause the hook after agent_is_reserved returns false, append the session reservation, resume the hook, and assert spawn_hook cannot run. Also assert attach does not merely fail while the responder runs.

Ownerless-claim refusal protects the logs, but it does not protect the already-running harness.

[risk:high] An active replacement can age out before it reaches occupy and then strip the predecessor claim. After append_session_if writes the pending successor, another session command can classify it as abandoned after 30 seconds and detach it at src/cli/sessions.rs:315-350. The paused attach still holds replaced_record, so occupy can transfer the predecessor claim to the detached successor at src/cli/sessions.rs:535-549. Its commit then fails at src/cli/sessions.rs:553-556, and release_owned at line 558 releases that transferred claim. The predecessor remains attached without occupancy.

Failure modes: a remote responder can start beside the predecessor, or claim consumers can treat the live identity as free.
Edge cases: a claims-lock stall, process suspension, slow storage sync, concurrent predecessor renewal, and reconciliation just before ownership transfer.
Rollback: disable replacement while an in-progress reservation can expire independently of its writer.
Monitoring: detect attached predecessors without one unexpired owned claim and claim releases caused by failed successor commits.
Validation: pause replacement before occupy for longer than PENDING_TTL_SECS, reconcile it from another command, resume it, and assert the predecessor remains attached with its original blocking claim.

Before transfer, revalidate the pending record under a compatible admission protocol. A failed commit after takeover must restore the predecessor owner instead of releasing occupancy.

[risk:high] Session occupancy changes bypass the Git auto-commit path. Attach, renew, detach, handback, and reconciliation append claims through append_claim_if or release_owned, but this module never calls auto_commit_after_claim or auto_commit_after_release. Ordinary claim stake and release do so at src/cli/claim.rs:246 and src/cli/claim.rs:709. rite sync push only pushes existing commits at src/sync/git.rs:289-315. Therefore a normal attach followed by sync push leaves the occupancy claim uncommitted and invisible to remote hosts. Renewals and detachments can also remain invisible.

Failure modes: another host cold-spawns the same agent, preserves an expired view while the session is live, or keeps a ghost claim after detach.
Edge cases: an already-initialized data Git repository, direct sync push, rapid attach and detach, and claim renewal without other auto-committed traffic.
Rollback: treat session occupancy as host-local only and disable cross-host admission claims until every transition has a durable sync contract.
Monitoring: report a dirty claims.jsonl after each session command and compare local claim tips with the pushed Git tip.
Validation: initialize two synced stores, attach and run sync push on the first, pull on the second, and assert the exact owned claim appears. Repeat for renew and detach without unrelated commands.

Use the established auto-commit path after each successful claim transition, with crash-safe ordering for the session record and commit result.

data.reason: BLOCK: three risk:high admission defects remain. Hook claim acquisition can spawn after a session reservation; a timed-out replacement can release its live predecessor occupancy; and session claim transitions do not enter the existing Git auto-commit path, so remote hosts can use stale admission state.
All successful occupancy transitions now use the established claims auto-commit path.
Failed and abandoned takeovers now hand occupancy back before any release.

data.body: [risk:high][resolved] The current target sends every successful session claim stake, extension, hand-back, and release through the existing auto-commit path at src/cli/sessions.rs:205-207, 231-233, 296-298, and 311-313. tests/sessions.rs:1532-1596 checks attach, renew, and detach commits. This resolves the reported bypass.

[risk:high][resolved] The failed-commit path now attempts hand_back before release at src/cli/sessions.rs:806-815. Reconciliation also returns a retired successor claim to its attached predecessor at src/cli/sessions.rs:393-410. The original retired-successor transfer no longer releases the predecessor occupancy.

[risk:high][still-open] The new reserve-before-launch flow is safe, but the public direct attach path remains. stake_hook_claim can read no reservation at src/cli/hooks.rs:1121-1129, then a direct attach can append its reservation at src/cli/sessions.rs:704-727 before the hook appends its ownerless claim. The hook then spawns at src/cli/hooks.rs:2095-2105. Attach only fails at src/cli/sessions.rs:784-797, after that harness already exists. AGENTS.md and src/cli/mod.rs:898-922 still advertise direct attach without this limitation.

Failure modes: two live harnesses use one agent identity, duplicate work, and send conflicting replies.
Edge cases: direct attach from the documented launcher, a message during attachment, TTL and on-exit hook claims, and attach failure after harness startup.
Rollback: require reserve-before-launch for responder-gated identities, or remove the duplicate-prevention promise from direct attach.
Monitoring: flag direct attach refusal when a hook claim was created after its reservation.
Validation: pause hook stake after the reservation read, perform direct attach reservation, resume the hook through spawn, and prove the already-live harness cannot overlap.

[risk:high] Binding a reservation does not verify that its occupancy claim is still live and owned by this attachment. Reserve accepts independent --ttl and --window values at src/cli/mod.rs:889-895. If the TTL expires before the longer window, bind_reservation still appends attached here because it checks only session-log state. A remote hook or another claim consumer can take agent://name after expiry, and this bind then reports success beside that holder.

Failure modes: two live agents share one identity, remote cold spawning, duplicate work, and conflicting replies.
Edge cases: --ttl shorter than --window, a slow harness start, expiry during bind, and another holder taking the pattern before commit.
Rollback: require the claim to outlive the reservation and revalidate or renew exact ownership before committing the session.
Monitoring: alert on any pending or attached record whose claim is absent, expired, or owned by another attachment.
Validation: reserve with a one-second TTL and a longer window, let the claim expire, stake the pattern elsewhere, then bind. Assert bind fails without an attached record, or atomically restores exclusive occupancy.

[risk:high] An unknown session event fails open. The wire decoder accepts a newer event as SessionEvent::Unknown here, so the log remains readable. is_reserved returns false for that latest record at src/core/session.rs:170-176, and reserved_for_agent ignores it at src/core/session.rs:370-375. After an upgrade writes a new live-state event, an older binary can therefore treat the identity as free and attach or spawn another agent.

Failure modes: version skew or downgrade starts a second agent beside a still-live session and permits conflicting work.
Edge cases: a future paused, reconnecting, or ownership-transfer event; mixed binaries on one host; and rollback after a partial deployment.
Rollback: treat an unknown latest lifecycle event as reserved or incompatible until its semantics are known.
Monitoring: report unknown latest session events as an admission-blocking compatibility fault.
Validation: append an unknown event after an attached record, then assert hook admission and a second attach both fail closed.

data.reason: Three risk:high blockers remain: direct attach can overlap a spawned responder, reservation binding can commit after occupancy expires, and unknown lifecycle events fail open.

data.body: [resolved] The direct-attach limitation is now explicit in src/cli/sessions.rs:28-35, src/cli/mod.rs:898-922, and AGENTS.md:97. The safe launcher contract reserves before starting the harness and then binds the session id. Direct attach now reports overlap when an ownerless responder claim won first.

data.reason: Accepted limitation is explicit; reserve-before-launch is the safe admission contract.

data.body: [resolved] Unknown latest events now reserve both agent and session identities at src/core/session.rs:180-185 and 379-410. Hook admission fails closed through agent_is_reserved at lines 336-348. Detach refuses unknown lifecycle state at src/cli/sessions.rs:974-979. tests/sessions.rs:1766-1840 covers second attach and hook admission.

data.reason: Unknown lifecycle events now remain admission-blocking and cannot be detached by this build.

data.body:
[risk:high][still-open] Claim ownership is checked from an unlocked snapshot at src/cli/sessions.rs:613-618. That check ends before the session commit at lines 633-639. The commit predicate checks only is_pending. It does not recheck claim ownership or reservation expiry. Also, src/cli/sessions.rs:499-505 permits --ttl to equal --window. Both can expire after claim_ok, another holder can stake agent://name, and bind can still append attached beside that holder. tests/sessions.rs:1678-1760 removes the claim before validation, so it does not cover this gap.

Failure modes: bind reports success for a live harness after exclusive occupancy moved to another agent. A responder and the harness can then perform duplicate work or send conflicting replies.
Edge cases: equal TTL and window, expiry between validation and append, a competing stake at that boundary, and delayed session-file locking or sync.
Rollback: do not use a bound reservation after its claim approaches expiry. Reserve again before launch until bind renews and validates ownership through commit.
Monitoring: alert when an attached record lacks one unexpired claim owned by its attachment. Correlate bind success with immediately preceding claim expiry or ownership change.
Validation: pause bind after line 618. Advance past claim expiry, stake agent://name elsewhere, resume, and assert no attached record commits. Also test equal TTL and window at the boundary.

data.reason: risk:high: reservation bind validates claim ownership before a race window, then commits without revalidation; th-2dbhdu remains open.

data.body:
[risk:high][still-open] The final recheck still does not fence the claim through the session append. bind_reservation renews with the caller supplied ttl_secs at src/cli/sessions.rs:624-632. The append predicate then reads claims without the claims lock at src/cli/sessions.rs:662-669. It also checks is_pending, but not is_abandoned, at lines 664-665. A bind can use a short TTL, pause after latest_claims returns, pass both the renewed claim expiry and pending_until, and let another claim command stake agent://name. The paused predicate still returns from its stale snapshot and appends attached beside the new holder.

Failure modes: bind reports success while another agent owns the identity. Both harnesses can perform duplicate work or send conflicting replies.
Edge cases: attach --ttl shorter than the original reserve window, a one-second TTL, process suspension, slow session-file fsync, and a competing stake at expiry.
Rollback: do not use bind as an exclusive admission fence until claim ownership remains locked through commit, or a recoverable rollback proves no attached state survives lost ownership.
Monitoring: alert on bind success after pending_until or claim expiry, and on attached records without one current owner-bound claim.
Validation: add a deterministic barrier after the claim read at line 666 and before the append. Bind with a short TTL, expire it, stake the identity elsewhere, resume, and assert no attached record commits. Repeat past pending_until.

data.reason: risk:high: reservation bind still checks claim ownership from an unlocked snapshot and can commit after the lease expires or changes hands; th-2dbhdu remains open.

data.body:
[risk:high][still-open] The new fence protects only writers that honor the open-file lock. commit_fenced locks the current claims descriptor at src/cli/sessions.rs:452-464, appends the attached record at src/cli/sessions.rs:468-472, then rechecks the same in-memory snapshot at src/cli/sessions.rs:476-478. rite sync pull runs git merge without that lock at src/sync/git.rs:392-397. Git can replace or rewrite claims.jsonl while the old descriptor remains locked. Bind can therefore commit against a stale inode and report success after the current claims path loses ownership or gains a competing holder.

Failure modes: bind reports success while another agent owns the identity, or while the reservation claim is released. Duplicate agents can perform duplicate work or send conflicting replies.
Edge cases: fast-forward merges, union merges, merge aborts, a competing claim with another id, a release for the same id, and path replacement after the first check.
Rollback: serialize sync pull with session and claim mutations through one stable lock. Until then, do not treat a successful bind as exclusive during sync.
Monitoring: alert when claims.jsonl identity changes during a session mutation. Also detect attached records without exactly one current, unexpired, owner-bound claim after each pull.
Validation: pause bind after the first claim check using pipe readiness and release. Run a merge that replaces claims.jsonl with released or competing state, then resume. Assert bind cannot leave an attached record. Verify the test observes the locked descriptor inode and the current path inode, without sleeps or probabilistic loops.

data.reason: risk:high: commit_fenced can validate a stale claims.jsonl inode while concurrent sync pull replaces the current path
